model.name: Version bump fires only from an explicit deploy action, atomic with a rebuild (never a post-commit hook)
model.description: A version bump belongs to an explicit DEPLOY action, never to a post-commit hook firing on arbitrary commits. MEASURED: a post-commit hook auto-bumped 0.8.116->0.8.117 on commit 43efc40ae — a PURE test-evidence commit (the tester's ROW raw output) with ZERO deploy intent. Two harms: (1) it destroys VERSION-AS-PROOF — the version no longer signals 'a deployable change went live', it moves on test noise, breaking the only mechanism that proves a fix shipped; (2) it can create INCONSISTENT builds — it bumps the source version unit + package.json post-commit but does NOT rebuild, so sw.js/dist can be left at the old stamp (this time consistent only by LUCK of a build landing, proven byte-identical after the fact, not by construction). The bump must fire ONLY from a deploy action and be ATOMIC with a rebuild.
model.family: intentless-automation — automatic machinery that acts WITHOUT explicit intent, invisible until it causes harm
familyInstances: (i) the server auto-minting units into scenario/index with NO policy (PII + traceability) -> R40.47
(ii) the server flushing the config unit -> the 0.8.54->0.8.46 version REGRESSION (R31.7 domain)
(iii) THIS post-commit hook auto-bumping the version on a non-deploy commit (43efc40ae test-evidence -> 0.8.116->0.8.117)

discoverySource.measured: post-commit hook bumped 0.8.116->0.8.117 on 43efc40ae (pure tester ROW test-evidence, zero deploy intent). Bumped source unit + package.json post-commit, no rebuild; dist happened to be byte-identical when the expert re-ran the build = luck, not construction.

model.crossRefNote: R31.7 = DRY single-source app version (the config-unit the family's instance (ii) regressed); R40.47 = same FAMILY (automatic machinery acting with no intent). This is the 3rd named instance of intentless-automation.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A version bump fires ONLY from an explicit DEPLOY action. The post-commit hook does NOT bump the version on any commit — committing is not a deploy.
A non-deploy commit (e.g. the test-evidence commit 43efc40ae) that results in a version bump => RED. Version-as-proof: it must not move on test noise.

Any version bump is ATOMIC with a rebuild — the source version unit + package.json + sw.js + dist move together or not at all; no partial bump that updates the stamp without producing the matching build.
Source/package version bumped while sw.js/dist stay at the OLD stamp => RED (the inconsistent-build harm made impossible by construction, not caught by luck-of-a-build).

The version is a PROOF signal: it moves IFF a deployable change actually went live. A rebuild that produces a byte-identical dist is NOT a deployable change and MUST NOT bump — preserving the only mechanism that proves a fix shipped.
